headline: Chips rip (SOX +6.9%) and oil sinks on Iran restraint; S&P 500 has its best day since April
summary: Stocks opened higher, with the S&P 500 printing its low at the open, and climbed most of the day as oil slid, closing just below the session high with a 2.3% gain. The rally was broad: all 11 S&P sectors rose, led by industrials and consumer discretionary at more than 3%, advancers beat decliners by more than three to one and the Russell 2000 outran the large caps with a 3.1% jump. The VIX dropped more than 22% to back below 20.
drivers: After last week's 12% plunge on data-center regulation fears, the SOX jumped 6.9% back above 10,000: AMD soared 13.3% on an Oppenheimer upgrade to outperform ($600 target) and a role in Google's new TPU 8tx systems, Broadcom rose 8.8%, Applied Materials 11%, Lam 10%, KLA 9%, Marvell 9% and Micron 6%. Chips outside Nvidia added roughly 0.7 point to the S&P 500 on their own.
Oil slides as Trump plays down new Iran strikes

Trump said renewed attacks on Iran were highly unlikely while talks progress, and WTI fell 4.4% to settle at $86.85 (Brent −5.9% to $92.57), the lowest since August. Cheaper oil eased inflation worries a day before CPI and lifted airlines, cruise lines and other fuel-sensitive cyclicals.
Nvidia sinks on probe into CEO Huang

Nvidia fell 4.3% to $178.67, after dropping nearly 9% early to its lowest since March 31, as its board opened an independent investigation into Jensen Huang following reports that a business executive he had a relationship with was gathering information for China. It was the only SOX member to fall, and money rotated into its rivals.

Tesla rose about 5%, Meta and Amazon about 5% after JPMorgan named them top internet picks, and Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet gained more than 2%. Treasury yields were little changed, the 10-year near 4.86%, so rates did not hold back the bounce.
week: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq have now risen two days in a row and the S&P sits about 3.4% below its October 6 record, after a week in which it fell 2.7% (its worst since April 2025) and the Nasdaq slid into a correction; futures still price roughly a 77–81% chance of a December Fed hike after Friday's strong payrolls.
watch: Next: October CPI on Tuesday (headline expected around 3.9% from 3.7%, core 2.8%) plus a 10-year note auction, then PPI on Friday, with Nvidia's board probe and any news on data-center limits still steering the AI and chip names.
